previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of psoriatic arthritis, diabetes, morbid obesity, and a chronic left leg ulcer was admitted for recurrent cellulitis with worsening erythema, pain, and swelling near the wound site. He was started on broad-spectrum IV antibiotics due to leukocytosis and concern for deep infection. Imaging revealed new fluid and air collections in the left calf, prompting surgical consultation. After clinical deterioration, he underwent incision and drainage of a subcutaneous abscess. Antibiotics were narrowed to IV ceftriaxone based on infectious disease recommendation, and a PICC line was placed for outpatient therapy. His warfarin was held initially due to an elevated INR of 4.5 but was restarted at 10 mg daily, achieving therapeutic anticoagulation. Azathioprine was discontinued to support wound healing. The patient improved clinically, with resolving infection, stable diabetes control, and reduced pain. He was discharged home with a 14-day course of IV antibiotics, follow-up arranged in infectious disease, rheumatology, and plastic surgery, and detailed instructions on PICC line safety and warning signs.
problems: Cellulitis and abscess of leg, except foot
Diabetes with neurological manifestations, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
Adrenal cortical steroids causing adverse effects in therapeutic use
Personal history of noncompliance with medical treatment, presenting hazards to health

Brief Hospital Course:
___ yo male with history of recent MSSA cellulitis presents with 
neck swelling, initially admitted to the MICU for airway 
monitoring, and subsequently diagnosed w/ b/l sialoadenitis w/ 
possible bacterial superinfection.  

# B/l Fatty Sialoadenitis - Initially admitted to MICU due to 
concern for respiratory compromise, given reports in the ED that 
patient began to have mild SOB during CT exam, received IV 
Dexamethasone and epinephrine. On initial presentation to the 
MICU, the patients exam and imaging was most consistent with 
sialoadenitis involing the parotid glands (although no obvious 
fat stranding or collection on CT). ID and ENT were consulted 
and agreed on antibiotic tx for suspected bacterial 
super-infection and multiple viral serolgies were sent. CMV, IgG 
Mumps, and EBV negative; IgM mumps pending at time of discharge. 
Initially covered with Vanco/Clinda (received dose of Zosyn in 
ED). On ___ day of admission in MICU, pt had worsening swelling, 
and was started on Vanco, Cefepime, and Clinda IV. While in the 
MICU, he had no signs of respiratory compromise (never 
intubated) and VSS with no fevers. Transferred to the medical 
floor once stabilized. Antibiotic on transfer were narrowed to 
Clindamycin IV, as per ID. He received a total 8 day course of 
Clindamycin. Pain controlled with Oxycodone. Prior to discharge, 
ID recommended d/c Clindamycin and ENT did not think there was a 
bacterial infection, could have been viral given chronic steroid 
use or a manifestation of TMJ/psoriatic arthritis - see below. 
While on the medicine floor and prior to discharge, he was 
afebrile (with no elevation of WBC), VSS, and no signs of 
respiratory distress.

# Psoriasis c/b Arthritis - On chronic Dexamethasone at home, 
failed multiple DMARDs. New rash developed on his chest and 
upper arms after IV dexamethasone in ED. Dermatology was 
consulted and given his h/o psoriasis, they concluded that it 
was likely pustular psoriasis, since outbreaks can occur when 
given high dose of dexamethasone episodically (even while on 
chronic steroids). Started on Clobetasol which helped improve 
the rash significantly. Final readings of skin scrapings were 
pending at time of discharge. Scheduled f/u appointment with 
Dermatology. Continued Dexamethasone 4.5mg PO QD while admitted; 
and ID recommended starting PCP ppx given chronic steroids.

# H/o Pulmonary Embolism - Diagnosed on last admission in 
___. Was on Warfarin 6mg PO QD as an outpt. INR 
supratherapeutic on admission at 4.8. Warfarin was initially 
held. Restarted on ___ when INR was 1.7 at 10mg PO QD. 
Eventually lowered dose to 4mg PO QD at time of discharge; INR 
was 2.7. Instructed to check his INR on ___ and send result 
to PCP office for optimization of Coumadin dosing. INR followed 
by PCP office, as per pt. Goal INR ___. Exact end date of 
anti-coagulation will be determined by PCP/Hematology. 
Anticipated end date will be in ___ for 6 months of 
anticoagulation.

# OSA - Patient was unable to wear CPAP machine due to edema. 
CPAP as tolerated. Tele at night for OSA.

# Diabetes - Last A1C in our system 7.9. Continued home regimen. 
Initially attempted control with titration of sliding scale 
which was unsuccessful. Patient has carb counted in the past and 
we transitioned to this method which helped control blood 
glucoses in a more acceptable range. Patient was instructed to 
make a f/up appointment with ___ at time of discharge.

# Recent ___ cellulitis - Did not appear acutely infected, 
healing well. Covered with Clindamycin as above. S/p 6 week tx 
with IV CEFTX w/ Bactrim tail. Wound Care c/s placed and made 
recommendations.

#HTN/CV - Initially, anti-hypertensives held on admission due to 
a lactate of 5 which responded to fluids. Responded well to 
Lasix IV diuresis since he was volume overloaded on transfer to 
the medical floor given fluids and eventually restarted home 
diuretics (labs from ___ AM were error, they showed an 
elevated creatinine). Restarted home Lisinopril prior to 
discharge. Continued Atorvastatin 80mg PO QD and Aspirin.

# Elevated Lactate - Lactate was 3 on admission and trended 
upward to 5. This normalized with fluids. Never febrile and had 
a mild WBC elevation on admission to 12. Low suspicion for 
sepsis, ?toxin related vasodilation from the suspected b/l 
sialoadenitis - improved with Clindamycin. 

# Elevated LDH - Likely related to parotid gland inflammation. 
Has had elevated LDHs in the past up to 500. No signs of LAD on 
CT neck making lymphoma less likely. Should be checked as outpt 
to ensure resolution after acute illness.  

# Keratoconus s/p bilateral corneal transplant - Continued home 
eye drops.  

Transitional Issues
- Patient was full code throughout this hospitalization
- F/u Mumps IgM - State Lab
- Please check LFTs (mild elevation of ALT on discharge) and LDH 
as outpatient
- He refused ___ services; to the best of our knowledge, pt has 
multiple services set up prior to this admission. We offered the 
___ services and he refused, pt instructed to call and resume 
services previously established for his leg ___
- Restarted PCP prophylaxis with ___ SS 1 tab QD, as per ID 
recs
- Admitted with supratherapeutic INR of 4. Coumadin was held and 
then restarted once INR below 2. Discharged on 4mg PO QD 
(instead of his dose on admission of 6mg PO QD). Pt states that 
is going to check his INR at home with his INR machine and call 
his PCP office with results.
